verification: Live discovery, shuffle preservation, keyboard removal, six-object tree, reset and mobile board checks passed
repairs: Discovery progress starts at zero and resets to zero.
Shuffle rearranges the available objects without erasing the learner's current arrangement.
The choice tree includes all selected objects, including the sixth object.
The two-choice tree is explicitly distinguished from the learner's r-choice count.
Object counts reject non-finite values and normalize fractions to integers.
Selection counts reject non-finite values and stay within the available objects.
Drag inputs must belong to the current object set and target a valid slot.
Used objects cannot be selected a second time.
Filled slots can be cleared with pointer or keyboard activation.
Slot labels describe their current object and removal action.
Discovery progress has an accessible name and an empty-history explanation.
Previous and Next links navigate to the adjacent lessons.
Slots wrap on narrow screens and controls show visible keyboard focus.
